title: Fan-out 3/hour continue-email bound is check-then-act; concurrent cross-vacancy claims all pass
evidence:
UPDATE application_draft
SET continue_token = COALESCE(continue_token, $3),
    last_link_sent_at = now()
WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  AND email = lower($2)
  AND submitted_at IS NULL
  AND erased_at IS NULL
  AND (
    last_link_sent_at IS NULL
    OR last_link_sent_at < now() - interval '10 minutes'
  )
  AND (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d2
    WHERE d2.email = lower($2)
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at IS NOT NULL
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
  ) < 3
RETURNING COALESCE(continue_token, '') AS continue_token;
detail: Concurrent claims for the same email on different vacancies update different rows (no lock interaction); each count subquery reads a statement-start snapshot, so K simultaneous requests all pass <3 and send. The 3/hour bound holds only sequentially — drafts planted on K vacancies burst K branded emails at a victim.
recommended_fix: Serialize per-recipient: take pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(lower($2))) before the UPDATE (or wrap count+stamp in one Serializable transaction) so concurrent claims observe each other's stamps.

title: 500-per-vacancy draft cap races concurrent inserts of distinct pairs
evidence:
INSERT INTO application_draft (vacancy_id, email, fields, continue_token)
SELECT $1::uuid, lower($2), $3::jsonb, $4
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid AND d.email = lower($2)
  )
  OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
detail: The count<500 guard reads the inserting statement's snapshot; two concurrent saves for distinct new (vacancy,email) pairs both pass and both insert, exceeding the cap by the concurrency degree. Soft abuse bound — overshoot only, no corruption.
recommended_fix: Accept and document the overshoot, or enforce atomically (per-vacancy advisory lock around draft insert, or a counter maintained under row lock).

title: Duplicate-application branch never strips a coexisting live draft
detail: A live draft can coexist with an application (no-JS/failed-save submit leaves no draft row, then a later visit INSERTs a fresh draft — the upsert INSERT has no application-existence check). This branch renders the duplicate page without stripping: draft PII lingers and continue emails loop resume→duplicate until vacancy close.
recommended_fix: Run the same fail-open strip_draft_on_submit on the DuplicateApplication branch, or add an application-existence guard to the upsert INSERT path.

title: Save endpoint answers ok:true when the upsert wrote zero rows (cap reject for a new pair)
detail: Zero-row upserts (500-cap reject for a new pair, alongside the deliberate submitted/erased guards) all hit Ok(_) → ok:true; the client reads body.ok as save-acknowledged (announceSaved), so a real applicant at the cap loses answers silently and the funnel can count a phantom draft.
recommended_fix: Distinguish why zero rows returned (reason column via CTE, or pre-check the cap for new pairs) and answer ok:false for the cap case; keep ok:true only for the submitted/erased no-op.
